newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close at new 37-month low.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close at new 37-month low.

text.p: Stocks closed at a 37-month low on Wednesday as rumours that Sammi Steel ran into financial trouble depressed sentiment, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed a provisional 715.87, down 9.72 points from Tuesday.

Rumours said Sammi sought $700 million in loans from the Korea Development Bank (KDB) to meet operating expenses and cover investment plans. Brokers said this sparked speculation about financial difficulties. Sammi officials declined comment.

Other rumours said Sammi was threatening to file a court receivership unless the loans were secured. Sammi Steel issued a statement saying the rumour that it was seeking court receivership was groundless. KDB officials declined comment.
Sammi spokesman Hwang Tae-kyu said the company was expected to post a fall in sales this year because of sluggish local demand. Sammi's sales totalled one trillion won in 1995.
Hwang declined further comment on its financial performance, but analysts said the company's net loss was expected to rise this year from 37 billion won in 1995.
Brokers said stock prices would fall further on Thursday in the absence of government boosting measures.

"The bottom seems to be at around 700 this year. If the level is broken, the government will intervene," said a Hyundai Securities broker. The government's possible boosting steps could include a plan to urge state-managed funds to increase stock investment, brokers said. Government officials refused to comment.
